decisions.reason: As a security-related feature that complements regulated-use-case platforms, it is not the firm's core strategic pillar but prior development effort and its fit with secure ecosystem offerings make management more likely to retain it than withdraw it.
An identity-bound payment wallet sits close to the firm's stated combination of identity, payments, and super-app convenience, so visible strategic fit and invested resources favor continuation.

Although authentication matches the firm's security positioning, an NFC-tag login method is comparatively niche and less central to the announced platform direction, making it the most vulnerable but still not the most likely to be dropped under escalation of commitment.
A secure payment and wallet framework has its own page and is strongly aligned with the firm's public super-app and ecosystem strategy, so management is likely to justify and continue the commitment.
This product is essentially at the heart of the firm's declared move toward secure multi-service mobile platforms, so its strategic centrality makes withdrawal very unlikely.

An application shielding library builds directly on the firm's long-standing security capabilities and public productization, so sunk investment and competence-based commitment support keeping it on the market.
